parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
From Source A, identify two countries where there has been an increase in the number
of people aged under 25 between 1975 and 2015.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Using information in Source A, explain two reasons why the data is useful for studying
population change in people aged under 25.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text:
Using information in Source A, explain three reasons why the data may not be useful
for understanding population change.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: State two stages in research design.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Explain one strength and one limitation of participant observation.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Evaluate the effectiveness of semi-structured interviews in sociological research.
Your answer should include:
• at least two arguments for and two arguments against
• a conclusion.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
Explain the research methods and evidence that you would choose to investigate age inequality
in the workplace. Give reasons for your choices.
Your answer should include:
• two primary methods with relevant sampling
• one source of secondary evidence. 
Answer either Question 2 or Question 3.
Identity: self and society

text: Read Source A and then answer the questions below.
Fig. 1.1 shows the number of people aged under 25 in selected countries. The data shows population
changes in these countries between 1975 and 2015. The secondary data in the chart was gathered
by the World Health Organisation (WHO). The WHO employs professional researchers to produce
its statistics using census data from each country. The researchers rounded data up or down to
population aged under 25 in selected countries
Source: adapted from the website ‘Our World in Data’.
